*OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes using perplexity, a measure of how accurately AI predicts text, to establish shared limits on AI development. Companies could agree not to advance beyond certain thresholds until their ability to understand and monitor AI behavior reaches defined safety milestones.*

• *Measuring Progress:* Pachocki argues that conventional AI benchmarks quickly become outdated, while perplexity remains useful for tracking advances in general intelligence. Lower perplexity indicates better prediction.
• *Emerging Capabilities:* He links declining model prediction losses to breakthroughs in reasoning, cybersecurity and mathematics, citing GPT-4's roughly 0.91 score and newer models falling below 0.8.
• *Industry Coordination:* Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has proposed common safety standards and limits on unchecked AI progress, drawing apparent support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk. Pachocki's measurement could provide a basis for such agreements.

*Meta's Alexandr Wang says superintelligence is arriving, citing what he describes as an AI-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a historic breakthrough. He warns that decisions made over the next year could determine whether humanity maintains control over increasingly powerful AI.*

• *AI Breakthrough:* Wang argues the mathematical achievement signals that raw intelligence is no longer AI's main limitation. Remaining barriers involve specialized knowledge, infrastructure and experimentation.
• *Expanding Capabilities:* He says AI has nearly solved coding and developed powerful cybersecurity and autonomous agent capabilities, potentially enabling major advances across scientific fields.
• *Self-Improving AI:* Wang predicts models could automate AI research and improve themselves, rapidly accelerating discoveries in biology, economics, weapons research and other fields beyond human oversight.
• *Human Control:* Wang warns that unrestricted AI self-improvement could become extremely difficult for humanity to control. He urges stronger safety, alignment and security measures while rejecting a societal “handover” to AI in favor of human agency.

*U.S. stock futures rebounded sharply Sunday evening, led by Nasdaq-100 futures, as Wall Street began a Thanksgiving-shortened week following a brutal technology-led selloff that pushed all three major indexes into correction territory.*

• *Futures Rebound:* Nasdaq-100 futures +2.67% at 25,797; S&P 500 futures +1.99% at 7,072.75; Dow futures +1.40%, or 675 points, at 48,891.
• *Market Selloff:* The S&P 500 lost 8.6% last week, while the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for 2026. Concerns over AI spending and investment returns continue despite Anthropic's record IPO.
• *Market Outlook:* Investors are watching whether the rebound signals a durable bottom or temporary relief. U.S. stock markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving, with Friday's session ending at 1 p.m. ET.

*The New York Times reports U.S. intelligence tracked Alice Huang's contacts with China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 through fall 2026, overlapping her affair with former Nvidia ($NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang and Megaspeed's chip acquisitions. Intelligence also reportedly shows her business partner, Kang Wei, worked with the same spy agency, strengthening U.S. suspicions that Jensen was targeted in a Chinese intelligence operation.*

• *Intelligence Findings:* Alice maintained contact with a Chinese intelligence officer for over a year and reportedly met officials from China's separate Ministry of Public Security, its main law enforcement agency. Kang, whom she often introduced as her husband, was also linked to intelligence work. The full extent of their activities remains unclear.
• *Chip-Smuggling Network:* U.S. intelligence reportedly includes shipping records documenting Alice and Kang's roles in Southeast Asian companies, including Megaspeed. Some Nvidia chips went to regional data centers serving Chinese companies, while others are suspected of being smuggled into China. Their network has also been linked to efforts to supply Chinese state-owned military contractors.
• *Broader Chinese Operation:* The findings connect the suspected chip network to China's wider push to overcome U.S. technology restrictions. Former U.S. Deputy National Security Adviser Matt Pottinger said the network “lines up precisely” with the Chinese spy agency's newly declared mission to circumvent export controls.
• *Trump Warnings:* U.S. officials say Trump was informed at least twice about Alice's intelligence ties and relationship with Jensen but downplayed the concerns and declined to intervene. Trump claims he was never informed. Nvidia's board has rejected his suggestion to reinstate Jensen.
• *Government Intelligence:* Secretary of State Marco Rubio detailed Alice's intelligence ties in a confidential March 30 memo, while Jensen never received a defensive intelligence briefing. Lawmakers from both parties are demanding more information after an earlier briefing raised questions and the administration postponed a follow-up session.

*Arm ($ARM) CEO Rene Haas signed a new contract keeping him at the company until 2033, weeks after Nvidia ($NVDA) approached him as a possible successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times reports.*

• *Long-Term Commitment:* Haas said Monday he was “wholly committed” to realizing Arm’s full potential for many years.
• *Nvidia Search:* The Financial Times reported earlier this month that Nvidia’s board approached Haas during its search for a new CEO.

*CrowdStrike ($CRWD) agreed to acquire Zscaler ($ZS) in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, combining two major cybersecurity platforms as businesses confront growing AI-related threats.*

• *Deal Terms:* Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, valuing Zscaler at $260.41 per share, a 34% premium.
• *Market Reaction:* Zscaler shares rose 12% in Monday premarket trading, while CrowdStrike fell 10%.
• *Combined Business:* The companies expect more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue at closing. They already share over 2,000 customers and would combine endpoint, cloud and network security.
• *Projected Benefits:* CrowdStrike expects $1 billion in annualized revenue synergies within 30 months of closing, largely from cross-selling, plus $500 million in annualized cost savings within 18–24 months.
• *Ownership and Timing:* CrowdStrike shareholders would own 84.1% of the combined company, with Zscaler investors holding 15.9%. Closing is expected in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028.

*Applied Digital agreed to provide ChronoScale Holdings a fully funded $97 million interest-free loan that will automatically convert into shares once required shareholder approval becomes effective, according to an SEC filing.*

• *Conversion Terms:* The loan converts at $8 per share into 12.125 million ChronoScale shares, subject to adjustments for stock splits and similar changes.
• *Ownership:* Applied Digital reports potential beneficial ownership of 151.65 million shares, or 85.6%, assuming conversion. Most shares are held through a wholly owned subsidiary.
• *Approval Timing:* Shareholders signed written consent on Nov. 18. Approval becomes effective 20 days after ChronoScale mails its definitive Schedule 14C information statement.

*Applied Digital ($APLD) closed a $300 million senior secured bridge financing facility to support construction of its Delta Forge 1 AI data center campus in Louisiana.*

• *Loan Terms:* The facility provides a delayed-draw loan with a 364-day maturity and interest at SOFR plus 300 basis points (3 percentage points). It is secured by project assets.
• *Funding Conditions:* Draws depend on construction milestones, regulatory approvals, including state approval of electricity rates, lender consents and financial covenants.
• *Customer Backing:* Delta Forge 1 is supported by a long-term lease with a U.S.-based, investment-grade hyperscaler.
• *Additional Financing:* Applied Digital expects to seek further funding to complete construction. The bridge loan can be repaid early without a premium.

*Nvidia’s ($NVDA) China business faces growing uncertainty after Jensen Huang’s resignation, with some Chinese customers cancelling chip orders amid fears of tighter U.S. export restrictions, Reuters reports.*

• *Cancelled Orders:* Chinese customers have begun cancelling RTX PRO 5500 orders over concerns about possible restrictions. Reuters could not determine the scale or whether either government would block shipments.
• *China Revenue:* Revenue from customers headquartered in China and Hong Kong more than tripled year over year, reaching $11.05 billion in the October 2026 quarter, up from $2.97 billion.
• *Chip Demand:* Chinese orders for RTX PRO 5500 exceed 6 million units, against projected worldwide production of up to 3 million in 2027. Deliveries were expected to begin early next year.
• *Robotics Exposure:* At least 14 Chinese robotics companies use Nvidia technology, according to a think tank. Limited domestic alternatives and high switching costs complicate efforts to replace Nvidia products.

*Taiwan stocks saw a record NT$49 billion ($1.5 billion) decline in margin loans Friday, the largest one-day leverage unwind in Bloomberg records dating to 1996.*

• *Borrowing Collapse:* Outstanding margin loans have fallen more than 30% from October's record high of approximately NT$653 billion, reflecting a sharp reduction in borrowed money used to buy stocks.
• *Market Selloff:* Taiwan's benchmark index fell 17.5% last week, its worst weekly decline since 1991, despite authorities' efforts to stabilize the market.
• *Margin-Call Risk:* Goldman Sachs warned that forced selling remains a threat. The market's maintenance margin ratio fell to 132%, near the 130% margin-call threshold, with 53% of stocks below that threshold.
• *AI Exposure:* Taiwan's earlier AI-driven rally reversed as investors grew concerned about the heavy spending required to expand AI infrastructure.

*Morgan Stanley's Michael Wilson says the U.S. stock selloff has created a compelling buying opportunity, citing cheaper valuations and improving earnings forecasts. His team is the most bullish tactically since April.*

• *Valuations:* The S&P 500's forward price-to-earnings ratio fell from nearly 23 in late October to 16.5, below its long-term average of 17.4. The index is 12% below its October high.
• *Earnings Disconnect:* Wilson estimates stocks are pricing in a 6% earnings decline for 2027, compared with Morgan Stanley's forecast of 14% growth and Wall Street's consensus of 17%.
• *Buying Opportunities:* Morgan Stanley favors hyperscalers, industrials, quality cyclical stocks with improving earnings forecasts, and companies benefiting from AI adoption.
• *Fed Risk:* A more aggressive Federal Reserve remains the biggest threat, but Wilson believes markets already reflect excessive tightening fears and expects a more measured Fed message in December.

*JPMorgan's U.S. trading desk has shifted from a tactically bullish to a cautious stock-market stance, warning that an expected rebound may not develop into a sustained rally.*

• *Outlook Shift:* Andrew Tyler says the desk misjudged Nvidia *($NVDA)* and capital-markets activity as support for a tech-sector bottom. Economic and earnings fundamentals remain intact.
• *Rally Risks:* Interest-rate uncertainty threatens earnings forecasts for 2027 and 2028. Uncertainty surrounding Nvidia and other technology companies makes a near-term market bottom less convincing.
• *Bullish Conditions:* Tyler wants lower volatility, a reset in investor positioning, cyclical stocks outperforming defensive shares, and the Fed delaying another rate hike beyond December.
• *Tech Rotation:* JPMorgan expects further movement away from technology stocks, but warns crowded rotation trades could suffer if tech rebounds.

*Applied Digital ($APLD) signed a new 18-year, 150 MW AI data center lease worth approximately $5.4 billion, bringing total contracted base-term lease revenue above $41 billion.*

• *Expanded Revenue:* Renewal options could increase the new lease's value to $12.7 billion over 33 years and total portfolio contracts to approximately $100 billion. The new lease carries higher pricing than previous agreements.
• *Portfolio Scale:* Contracted critical IT capacity now exceeds 1.6 GW, with 2.2 GW of grid-connected peak load. Investment-grade tenants account for approximately 75% of base-term contracted revenue.
• *Financing Plans:* Applied Digital plans to use its $5 billion Macquarie equity partnership and project financing. It expects to complete financing for Delta Forge 1 and Polaris Forge 3 in Q1 2027, followed by Delta Forge 2 in Q2.
• *Delivery Timeline:* Capacity delivery is expected to begin in the first half of 2028, subject to development milestones, utility arrangements and regulatory approvals.

*U.S. homebuyer interest fell to its lowest level since Zillow ($Z) began tracking in 2023, as engaged shoppers per listing dropped 4.8% year over year to 3.5 in Q3 2026.*

• *Mortgage Pressure:* Rates climbed from 6.43% in July to 7.28% by Oct. 1, raising monthly payments. For-sale inventory increased year over year for 35 consecutive months.
• *Widespread Decline:* Buyer engagement fell in 44 of the 50 largest metros, led by Seattle (-17.1%), Washington, D.C. (-15.5%) and Louisville (-14.3%).
• *Regional Differences:* Buffalo, Hartford, Providence and San Francisco had the highest engagement. Four of the six metros reporting annual increases were in Florida.
• *Luxury vs. Starter:* Luxury listings attracted 6.4 engaged shoppers each, more than double starter homes at 2.9. Starter-home engagement fell 8.2% year over year.
• *Rental Demand:* Rental interest rose 22.1% annually, including a 24.3% increase for single-family homes, as Zillow reported signs of prospective buyers shifting toward renting.

*CrowdStrike ($CRWD) beat Q3 FY2027 earnings estimates, reported record new annual recurring revenue (ARR), and raised its full-year outlook alongside its announced $43.9 billion Zscaler acquisition.*

• *Earnings Beat:* Revenue rose 28% year over year to $1.58 billion, above $1.53 billion expected. Adjusted EPS reached $0.34 versus $0.31 estimated.
• *Record ARR:* Ending ARR grew 27% to $6.26 billion. Net new ARR jumped 58% to a record $419.2 million.
• *Raised Guidance:* FY2027 revenue is now forecast at $6.078–$6.084 billion, with ending ARR of $6.712–$6.716 billion. Expected net new ARR growth increased to 45% at the midpoint.
• *Zscaler Acquisition:* CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler *($ZS)* for $43.9 billion in stock, offering 1.135 shares per Zscaler share. Management expects immediate free-cash-flow-per-share accretion upon closing, before synergies.
• *Cash Flow and AI:* Free cash flow rose 60% to $474.4 million. Adjusted operating income increased 53% to $405.5 million, while Falcon Guardian surpassed $100 million in ARR shortly after quarter-end.

*Zscaler ($ZS) reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $949.3 million, up 20% year over year, beating estimates alongside stronger adjusted earnings and 21% annual recurring revenue growth.*

• *Earnings Beat:* Adjusted EPS rose 28% to $1.23 versus $1.16 expected, beating FactSet consensus by 6.03%.
• *Revenue Beat:* Sales increased from $788.1 million to $949.3 million, exceeding the $937.7 million consensus by 1.24%.
• *Recurring Revenue:* ARR reached $3.882 billion, up 21% year over year. Net new ARR totaled $111 million.
• *Cash Flow:* Operating cash flow reached $541 million, while free cash flow totaled $416.5 million.
• *Acquisition Impact:* Zscaler withdrew financial guidance and cancelled its earnings call following CrowdStrike's announced $43.9 billion acquisition.

*Deutsche Bank forecasts the S&P 500 reaching 9,000 by year-end 2027 and the STOXX 600 hitting 750 by Q4, while raising its U.S. dollar outlook on AI-driven economic strength.*

• *Growth Forecasts:* Deutsche Bank projects 2027 global GDP growth of 3.5%, with U.S. growth at 2.3% and euro-area growth at 1.2%.
• *Dollar Outlook:* The bank expects the dollar to remain elevated through 2027, strengthening into the first half before modest weakening later in the year.
• *AI Support:* Deutsche Bank says AI investment is supporting higher U.S. real interest rates, equity inflows and inflation pressures, reinforcing a more hawkish Federal Reserve and dollar strength.
• *Downside Risks:* A sharp reduction in AI capital spending could weaken U.S. rates and equity inflows. The bank also notes growing investment shifts toward foreign bonds.

*Arm ($ARM) CEO Rene Haas extended his contract through 2033, declining a potential move to lead Nvidia ($NVDA) after executive recruiters approached him about replacing Jensen Huang.*

• *Haas Commitment:* “I’ve never been more confident about Arm’s future,” Haas said. “I’m incredibly proud of what we’re building and wholly committed to realizing Arm’s full potential for many years to come.”
• *SoftBank Appointment:* Haas will also become vice chairman of SoftBank, Arm's largest shareholder, effective Dec. 1. He previously spent seven years at Nvidia.
• *Other Candidates:* Potential Nvidia CEO successors include Nvidia VP Ian Buck, AMD *($AMD)* CEO Lisa Su and Apple *($AAPL)* Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji.
• *Leadership Search:* Nvidia's board has said it does not intend to reinstate Huang despite calls from Trump. CFO Colette Kress continues as interim CEO.

*Fermi ($FRMI) confirmed that its customer prepayment agreement has been fulfilled and the funds received, advancing its proposed 600 MW AI data center development at Project Matador in Texas.*

• *Payment Confirmed:* Fermi's Nov. 23 SEC filing confirms funding under the previously announced $200 million prepayment agreement with an investment-grade hyperscaler.
• *Payment Timing:* Fermi previously said the full $200 million was due Nov. 13. Today's filing does not specify when the funds arrived.
• *Construction Plans:* The funding supports the proposed 600 MW development. Fermi previously targeted Dec. 1 to begin site mobilization, with initial power expected in 2027.
• *Still Pending:* The filing does not confirm a definitive long-term lease, identify the customer or update the separate $90 million materials agreement.

*Klarna expanded its partnership with Visa, making its flexible payment options available to merchants using Visa Acceptance Platform across the U.S., Canada, U.K. and Europe.*

• *Merchant Integration:* Businesses can now offer Klarna through their existing Visa payment infrastructure without building or maintaining a separate integration.
• *Payment Options:* Customers can choose to pay in full, use interest-free installments or access longer-term financing at checkout.
• *Expanded Reach:* The integration gives Klarna access to Visa's existing merchant network, which serves hundreds of thousands of businesses.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

*Nvidia ($NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately, following a unanimous board vote.*

• *Board Review:* Directors approved Huang's return after discussions assessing his candor and leadership ability. Harvey Jones remains board chair, while interim CEO Colette Kress continues as CFO.

• *National Security:* The board says input from senior U.S. government officials gave it confidence that Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.

• *Intelligence Probe:* An independent board committee will continue investigating reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Huang has pledged full cooperation.

• *Compliance Oversight:* Nvidia established a National Security and Export Control Committee to oversee trade compliance and security risks, supported by specialized legal counsel and advisers.

• *New Compliance Chief:* Nvidia is recruiting a Chief Compliance Officer to oversee company-wide compliance and report to the board's Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. The company will also cooperate with ongoing government investigations.

Nvidia: “In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”
